KNOWN BUG: Clearing the combobox never calls onChange(null), so the selection can't be cleared.

Rules:
- Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no".
- A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no".
- Wording does not matter; the behaviour does.
- For handoffs: count only text that tells the implementor to fix this bug (a reported finding, a fix instruction). Restated acceptance criteria that merely describe the desired behaviour do NOT count as carrying the finding unless the handoff ties them to a reported failure.

=== REVIEW 1 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] Dialog trap escapes when focus is on body (D3, D4). The `onKeyDown` trap only runs when `content.contains(event.target)`, so with focus on body Tab goes to the page. Repro 1 (focused button removed mid-dialog, then Tab): `expect(dlg.contains(document.activeElement)).toBe(true)` fails, active element is `<button>behind</button>`. Repro 2 (parent ignores close, user clicks backdrop, then Tab): `R1 focus after backdrop click: BODY`, then `R1 focus after Tab: behind`.
- [blocking] Dialog Escape does nothing when focus is on body (D4). Repro: `(document.activeElement as HTMLElement).blur(); await user.keyboard("{Escape}")` gives `expected "spy" to be called with arguments: [ false ] ... Number of calls: 0`. Same root cause as above: Escape is only handled on the content element.
- [blocking] Tabs roving tabindex goes stale when tabs change inside a child component (T3, T6, hostile "conditional Tab"). `TabList`'s layout effect only re-runs when TabList re-renders, so a child-owned `<Tab>` that unmounts leaves no tab with tabIndex 0. Repro: `<TabList><Tab value="a"/><Child/></TabList>` with `defaultValue="x"`, then Child removes `x`. Result: `A tabindex after X removed: -1`, and `await user.tab()` lands on the tabpanel, skipping the tablist. Reproduced again when a child adds a tab while the list had no enabled tab: `R2 N tabindex: -1`, Tab does not reach N. The parent-rerender case works (tabIndex 0 on A), so the failure is specific to child-owned tabs. Fix idea: have Tab register/unregister in a `useLayoutEffect` with the context, or compute activeId from a state set in Tab's own effects.
- [minor] Keyboard from a focused disabled tab is stuck. Clicking a `disabled` tab focuses it (only `aria-disabled` is set, so the button stays focusable). Repro: click disabled "A", then `ArrowRight` leaves focus on "A". Tab still leaves, and the spec does not require the tab to be unfocusable, so this is minor.
- [minor] `<Combobox defaultValue="x">` passes `defaultValue` through the `rest` spread alongside `value`, so React logs "contains an input of type text with both value and defaultValue props". `ComboboxProps` should also omit `defaultValue`.
- [minor] Controlled Tabs whose parent ignores `onValueChange`: arrow keys move DOM focus to a tabIndex -1 tab while the selected tab keeps tabIndex 0. Behavior is consistent with the criteria, but the README does not say so.
=== REVIEW 2 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] Dialog focus on open lands on the wrong element when the content contains a Tabs. The Dialog's passive effect runs before TabList's layout-effect `setActiveId` updates tabIndex, so the first focusable is the panel (tabindex=0) and not the selected tab. Reproduced for a Dialog toggled open and for one initially open: `expect(document.activeElement).toBe(getByRole("tab",{name:"B"}))` got `<div role="tabpanel" id="…-panel-b">`. Violates D2. Combobox-in-Dialog focus is unaffected.
- [blocking] Tab's layout effect deps are `[disabled, notify]`, so changing a child-owned Tab's `value` in place never notifies Tabs. The tablist then has no tabIndex=0 tab (activeId is stale). Reproduced: a `Kid` component renders `<Tab value={v}>` and calls `setV("q")`; `zeros.length` was 0, expected 1. Violates the T3/T6 requirement that some tab stays tabIndex=0. Fix: add `value` to the effect deps.
- [minor] Tabs: when the selected tab is removed by a child component while uncontrolled, aria-selected is absent everywhere while tabIndex falls back to the first enabled tab. Not reproduced as a keyboard failure; cosmetic.
=== IMPLEMENTOR HANDOFF 1 (sent after review 1) ===
GOAL: Fix reproduced defects in the uncommitted component library in /tmp/ff-eval-2i0c73o6/workspace (src/Dialog/Dialog.tsx, src/Tabs/Tabs.tsx, src/Combobox/Combobox.tsx, README.md). Add a regression test for each fix in the matching *.test.tsx, using user-event.

FILES: src/Dialog/Dialog.tsx (trap and Escape live in the content div's onKeyDown; trap only acts if content.contains(event.target)); src/Tabs/Tabs.tsx (TabList's no-deps useLayoutEffect derives activeId from DOM; reruns only when TabList rerenders); src/Combobox/Combobox.tsx; tests next to each; README.md.

FIXES REQUIRED:
1. [blocking] Dialog: when focus is on body (e.g. the focused button was removed while open, or the user clicked the backdrop while the parent ignores onOpenChange), Tab goes to elements behind the dialog and Escape does nothing. Fix:
   - Keep a module-level stack of open dialogs (push in the open effect, remove in its cleanup) so only the topmost dialog acts on document-level events.
   - Add a document `focusin` listener (while open, topmost only): if focus moves to an element outside the content (and outside any dialog content above it — topmost check covers this), move focus back to the first focusable in the content, or the content itself.
   - Add a document `keydown` listener (topmost only) handling events whose target is NOT inside the content (e.g. body): Escape → onOpenChange(false); Tab/Shift+Tab → preventDefault and focus first/last focusable (or content). Keep the existing content onKeyDown handling for events inside (Escape with stopPropagation so a Combobox's open-listbox Escape still only closes the listbox, nested dialogs still close one at a time).
   - Backdrop: `onMouseDown={e => e.preventDefault()}` so a backdrop click doesn't move focus to body.
   - Use a ref for the latest onOpenChange so listeners don't need re-subscribing. Existing focus-restore behavior (on close/unmount, if previous element is connected) must still work, including nested dialogs restoring to the trigger inside the outer dialog — make sure the outer dialog's focusin listener doesn't steal focus while the inner one is topmost, and that when the inner closes and restores focus to its trigger inside the outer, nothing breaks.
2. [blocking] Tabs: a `<Tab>` owned by a child component that mounts/unmounts (or toggles disabled) leaves no tab with tabIndex 0. Repro: `<Tabs defaultValue="x"><TabList aria-label="t"><Tab value="a">A</Tab><Child/></TabList>...` where Child renders `<Tab value="x">` and then removes it via its own state; afterwards A has tabindex -1 and `user.tab()` skips the tablist. Also: child adds an enabled tab when the list had no enabled tab. Fix: have each Tab notify the Tabs context in a `useLayoutEffect` on mount, unmount and `disabled` change (e.g. a `version` counter state in Tabs bumped by a `notify` function), so TabList re-renders and its layout effect recomputes activeId.
3. [minor] Tabs: arrow keys from a focused disabled tab (clicking a disabled tab focuses it) do nothing. Make the key handler find the current index among ALL tabs and move to the next/previous enabled tab from there (wrapping), Home/End to first/last enabled.
4. [minor] Combobox: `ComboboxProps` must also omit `defaultValue` (and `defaultChecked` isn't relevant) from InputHTMLAttributes so it can't be passed alongside value.
5. [minor] README Tabs section: document that with controlled `value` and a parent that ignores onValueChange, arrow keys move focus but selection and tabIndex=0 stay on the selected tab. Document the Dialog focusin behavior (focus that leaves the dialog is pulled back in) and that a backdrop click doesn't move focus.

CONSTRAINTS: No new deps, no CSS. Don't change other public props or ARIA output. Don't touch FEATURE_FLOW.md, package.json, configs.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
General
- G1. `src/index.ts` exports Tabs, TabList, Tab, TabPanel, Dialog, Combobox and their props types (TabsProps, TabListProps, TabProps, TabPanelProps, DialogProps, ComboboxProps, ComboboxOption). No new dependencies, no CSS.
- G2. All IDs come from `React.useId()`; two instances of each component on one page have no duplicate IDs and independent state.
- G3. Extra HTML props and `className` pass through to the main element of each part (Tabs root div, TabList, Tab button, TabPanel, Dialog content element, Combobox input).
- G4. Tests in `src/Tabs/Tabs.test.tsx`, `src/Dialog/Dialog.test.tsx`, `src/Combobox/Combobox.test.tsx` drive components with `@testing-library/user-event`; one test per criterion below at least. `pnpm test` and `pnpm typecheck` pass.
- G5. README.md documents each component: a props table (name, type, default, description), a keyboard table, and a short usage example. README claims match the code.

Tabs
- T1. `<Tabs defaultValue? value? onValueChange?>`: uncontrolled with defaultValue; controlled with value (selection only changes when parent updates value; onValueChange is still called). If neither value nor defaultValue given, the first non-disabled tab is selected.
- T2. TabList has role="tablist", takes aria-label (required in its props type), aria-orientation="horizontal".
- T3. Tab is a `<button type="button" role="tab">` with aria-selected, aria-controls = its panel id, id referenced by the panel's aria-labelledby. Selected tab tabIndex=0, all others tabIndex=-1. Disabled tab has aria-disabled="true" (and stays focusable-by-script is not required), cannot be selected by click or keyboard.
- T4. TabPanel has role="tabpanel", aria-labelledby its tab, tabIndex=0; only the selected panel is shown (others rendered with `hidden` attribute or not rendered — pick one, document it).
- T5. ArrowRight/ArrowLeft move focus to next/previous enabled tab, wrapping at ends, skipping disabled ones; Home/End move to first/last enabled tab. Selection follows focus (moving focus selects and calls onValueChange). Keys preventDefault. Other keys do nothing.
- T6. Tab order: Tab key from before the tablist lands on the selected tab; next Tab press leaves the tablist (to the panel).
 Hostile inputs:
  - all tabs but one disabled: arrows keep focus on the one enabled tab; no infinite loop when every tab is disabled.
  - defaultValue/value naming a disabled or nonexistent tab: no crash, and some tab must still be tabIndex=0 — if the value matches no enabled tab, the first enabled tab gets tabIndex=0 so the list stays reachable.
  - tabs added/removed dynamically (conditional `<Tab>`): keyboard order follows DOM order after the change.
  - controlled value where parent ignores onValueChange: arrow key moves focus? Selection stays; document behavior (focus may move but aria-selected doesn't change).

Dialog
- D1. `<Dialog open onOpenChange title description? children>`; when open=false nothing is rendered. When open, rendered via `createPortal` into document.body: a backdrop element and a content element with role="dialog", aria-modal="true", aria-labelledby → title element (rendered as heading h2), aria-describedby → description element only when description is given (attribute absent otherwise).
- D2. On open, focus moves to the first focusable element inside the dialog content; if none, to the dialog content element itself (tabIndex=-1).
- D3. Focus trap: Tab from the last focusable wraps to the first, Shift+Tab from the first wraps to the last; with zero focusables, Tab keeps focus on the dialog. Focus cannot reach elements behind the dialog via Tab.
- D4. Escape calls onOpenChange(false). Clicking (pointer down + up) on the backdrop calls onOpenChange(false); clicking inside the content does not, and a drag that starts inside the content and ends on the backdrop does not close.
- D5. When the dialog closes (open goes false or the Dialog unmounts), focus returns to the element focused before opening, if it's still in the document.
- D6. Dialog is controlled only: if parent ignores onOpenChange(false), it stays open.
 Hostile inputs:
  - nested dialog (dialog opened from inside a dialog): Escape closes only the topmost; focus returns to the trigger inside the outer dialog.
  - the trigger was removed from the DOM while open: closing doesn't throw.
  - disabled buttons / tabindex="-1" elements / hidden inputs inside are skipped by the trap.
  - content changes while open (focusables added) — trap uses the current set at keypress time.
  - Body scroll lock is optional; if added, it must be restored on close.

Combobox
- C1. `<Combobox label options value onChange placeholder?>`; options `{ value: string; label: string; disabled?: boolean }`; value is `string | null`; onChange(value: string | null). The component is controlled for value (document it). A visible `<label>` associated with the input.
- C2. Input has role="combobox", aria-expanded (true/false), aria-controls → listbox id, aria-autocomplete="list", aria-activedescendant → active option's id only while the listbox is open and an option is active (absent otherwise). Listbox has role="listbox" and aria-labelledby the label; options have role="option", unique ids, aria-selected=true on the one matching value, aria-disabled="true" on disabled ones.
- C3. When closed, input shows the selected option's label (empty if value null or unknown). Typing opens the listbox and filters options whose label contains the input text case-insensitively (substring). Empty text shows all options.
- C4. ArrowDown opens the listbox if closed; when open moves the active option to the next enabled one; ArrowUp to the previous enabled one. Disabled options are skipped. Wrap at ends (document it). Active option resets when the filter text changes.
- C5. Enter on an active option calls onChange(option.value), closes the listbox, and sets the input text to the option label. Enter with no active option does nothing (no form submit prevention required beyond when listbox is open with an active option). Clicking an enabled option selects it; clicking a disabled option does nothing.
- C6. Escape closes the listbox without calling onChange and restores the input text to the selected option's label. (Escape when already closed: optional clear; document behavior.)
- C7. When the filter matches no options, the popup shows "No results" (not role="option"), announced to assistive tech (e.g. role="status" or inside the listbox area with aria-live polite); aria-activedescendant absent.
- C8. Blur (focus leaves the input, not into the listbox via mouse) closes the listbox and restores the input text to the selected label. Mouse down on an option must not blur-close before the click selects (use onMouseDown preventDefault).
- C9. If the user clears the input text completely and blurs/presses Enter with no active option, the value becomes null via onChange(null) (document it) — or keep it; whichever, document and test it.
 Hostile inputs:
  - all options disabled: ArrowDown opens but no active option, Enter does nothing, no infinite loop.
  - empty options array: shows "No results".
  - typed text with regex characters like "(" or ".*": treated as literal text, no crash.
  - option labels that differ only in case; value not in options (no crash, input empty).
  - parent rerenders with new `options` array identity each render: no infinite loop, active option stays valid.
  - two Comboboxes on the page: option ids don't collide.

CHECKS: while working `pnpm vitest run src/Dialog` / `src/Tabs`; at the end `pnpm test` and `pnpm typecheck`, both must pass.
